items.title: Dan Wall and Adam Nussbaum interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, April 19, 2001
items.q: The last record we did actually was I think John wrote maybe everything on the record the thing with Lovano and Kenny Wheeler and Mark Feldman.

ctx.x: Yeah, is a standard off the record. Two of ten cuts were standards I think. And one of those standards, because, I mean it works which is great, it has a simple — you know people like hearing standards from the organ and the whole thing. But this band has been very original. The last record we did actually was I think John wrote maybe everything on the record the thing with Lovano and Kenny Wheeler and Mark Feldman. I think there was one track we did a free track.

And there were quite a few free pieces. I mean many people, they look at an organ trio and they think the instrumentation will dictate the conception of the music and oh yeah, man, you guys play a lot of blues or you play a lot of this or a lot of that. Well no we don’t. We just, this is the instrumentation but we have our own approach to how we want to play. And we’ve never really discussed the concept of what we do, we just do it. And we all just listen to each other and whatever happens happens.
